title: The Normal-Distribution Normalization Family (from the Gaussian Integral)
description: Completes the Gaussian-integral strand of the area-of-circle lineage by deriving the normalization constants of the normal distribution — the rescalings of √π that turn the Gaussian into a probability density. The parent area-of-circle-oq-05 proves ∫ e^{-x²} = √π and connects it to circle area; siblings cover the polar proof, the multivariate case, and the complex Gaussian. None cover the normal-density normalization. From Mathlib's integral_gaussian this entry proves: ∫ e^{-x²/2} = √(2π) (gaussian_half); the standard-normal normalization ∫ (1/√(2π))e^{-x²/2} = 1; the general-variance integral ∫ e^{-x²/(2σ²)} = σ√(2π) for σ>0; the N(0,σ²) normalization ∫ (1/(σ√(2π)))e^{-x²/(2σ²)} = 1; the base case √π and the area identity (∫ e^{-x²})² = π; and mean-shift invariance ∫ e^{-(x-μ)²/2} = √(2π) (translation invariance of the integral). 8 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms (no native_decide).

meta.author: Gauss (Gaussian integral); classical normal-distribution normalization — formalized in Lean 4
originalContributions: Axiom-free derivation of the normal-distribution normalization constants from Mathlib's integral_gaussian: ∫ e^{-x²/2} = √(2π) and the general ∫ e^{-x²/(2σ²)} = σ√(2π)
The standard-normal and N(0,σ²) normalizations ∫ (1/√(2π))e^{-x²/2} = 1 and ∫ (1/(σ√(2π)))e^{-x²/(2σ²)} = 1, the probability-density statements the area-of-circle Gaussian integral underwrites
Mean-shift invariance ∫ e^{-(x-μ)²/2} = √(2π) via translation invariance of the Lebesgue integral (integral_sub_right_eq_self) — the density has the same mass for every mean
The base case √π and the squared identity (∫ e^{-x²})² = π restated to anchor the family in the area-of-circle context
meta.assumptions: None. Every theorem is derived from Mathlib's integral_gaussian by elementary algebra (sqrt manipulations, integral_const_mul, translation invariance); the variance statements take σ > 0 as an ordinary hypothesis. No axiom declarations, no native_decide, no sorries. #print axioms on the normalization and mean-shift theorems reports only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The parent area-of-circle-oq-05 is already complete; this entry (claimed as a 'completion' task) supplies the genuinely uncovered normal-density normalization strand rather than patching the parent.

overview.historicalContext: The Gaussian integral ∫_{-∞}^{∞} e^{-x²} dx = √π is the analytic heart of both the area-of-circle lineage (its square is computed as a 2D integral via polar coordinates, giving π) and probability theory (it normalizes the bell curve). The parent area-of-circle-oq-05 establishes the integral and the circle connection; its siblings formalize the polar proof, the multivariate Gaussian, and the complex Gaussian. The one classical strand left implicit is the chain of rescalings that turn e^{-x²} into the probability density of N(μ, σ²): the constants √(2π) and σ√(2π). This entry makes that chain explicit and axiom-free.
overview.problemStatement: From the Gaussian integral ∫ e^{-x²} = √π, derive the normalization constants of the normal distribution: ∫ e^{-x²/2} = √(2π), ∫ e^{-x²/(2σ²)} = σ√(2π), and the probability-density normalizations ∫ (1/√(2π))e^{-x²/2} = 1 and ∫ (1/(σ√(2π)))e^{-x²/(2σ²)} = 1, together with mean-shift invariance — all machine-checked, 0-axiom.
overview.text: Each result is a rescaling of Mathlib's integral_gaussian b : ∫ e^{-b x²} = √(π/b). Taking b = 1 recovers √π (gaussian_unit), b = 1/2 gives √(π/(1/2)) = √(2π) (gaussian_half), and b = 1/(2σ²) gives √(π/(1/(2σ²))) = √(2πσ²) = σ√(2π) for σ > 0 (gaussian_variance, using Real.sqrt_mul and Real.sqrt_sq). Each integrand is matched to integral_gaussian's exact form -b·x² by a pointwise ring/field_simp rewrite. The normalizations std_normal_normalization and gaussian_variance_normalization pull the constant out with integral_const_mul and cancel against the integral via inv_mul_cancel₀ (the constants are positive, e.g. sqrt_two_pi_pos). gaussian_unit_sq restates (∫ e^{-x²})² = π, the area-of-circle identity. gaussian_mean_shift uses translation invariance of the Lebesgue integral (integral_sub_right_eq_self) to show the mass is independent of the mean μ.
overview.proofStrategy: Reduce every statement to integral_gaussian at the right rate b, then do elementary algebra: pointwise matching of the integrand (ring/field_simp inside the exponent), √ simplification for the variance constant, pull-out-and-cancel for the normalizations, and translation invariance for the mean shift. No new integral is computed from scratch.
keyInsights: The bell curve's normalization constants are not new integrals — they are √π evaluated at different rates b in ∫ e^{-b x²} = √(π/b): b = 1/2 gives √(2π), b = 1/(2σ²) gives σ√(2π).
Pulling the constant out (integral_const_mul) and cancelling against the integral is all that separates the integral identities from the probability-density normalizations.
The variance constant σ√(2π) comes from √(π/(1/(2σ²))) = √(σ²·2π) = σ√(2π), needing only σ ≥ 0 to take √(σ²) = σ.
Translation invariance of the Lebesgue integral makes the normalization independent of the mean μ, so the full N(μ, σ²) family is normalized once σ is fixed.
The squared identity (∫ e^{-x²})² = π keeps the probabilistic family anchored to its geometric origin — the area swept out in the polar-coordinate proof.
prerequisites: The Gaussian integral ∫ e^{-x²} = √π and Mathlib's integral_gaussian
The normal distribution N(μ, σ²) and its density
Translation invariance of the Lebesgue integral

sections.title: Setup: the Gaussian import and the normalization-constant positivity lemma
sections.summary: The docstring situates this entry as the missing normal-distribution-normalization strand of the area-of-circle Gaussian lineage. Imports Mathlib's Gaussian-integral API and opens Real/MeasureTheory. sqrt_two_pi_pos proves 0 < √(2π) by positivity — the nonvanishing side condition every later normalization theorem needs to legally cancel the constant 1/√(2π) or 1/(σ√(2π)) against the integral value.
sections.mathContext: $\sqrt{2\pi} > 0$, proved by \texttt{positivity}; the nonvanishing constant every reciprocal-normalization theorem below depends on.

sections.title: Base case and the area identity
sections.summary: gaussian_unit (∫ e^{-x²} = √π, the parent's result re-derived from integral_gaussian at rate b=1) and gaussian_unit_sq ((∫ e^{-x²})² = π, the area-of-circle identity that the polar-coordinate proof computes as a 2D integral).

sections.title: Unit-variance normalization (the σ = 1 case)
sections.summary: gaussian_half (∫ e^{-x²/2} = √(2π), integral_gaussian at rate b=1/2) and std_normal_normalization (∫ (1/√(2π))e^{-x²/2} = 1) — the standard-normal density integrates to 1.

sections.title: General-variance normalization (σ > 0)
sections.summary: gaussian_variance (∫ e^{-x²/(2σ²)} = σ√(2π), via √(σ²·2π) = σ√(2π)) and gaussian_variance_normalization (∫ (1/(σ√(2π)))e^{-x²/(2σ²)} = 1) — the N(0,σ²) density integrates to 1 for every σ > 0.

sections.title: Mean-shift invariance
sections.summary: gaussian_mean_shift: ∫ e^{-(x-μ)²/2} = √(2π) for every mean μ, via translation invariance of the Lebesgue integral — the full N(μ,σ²) family is normalized.

crossReferences.description: The parent proves ∫ e^{-x²} = √π and the circle connection. This entry derives the normal-distribution normalization constants (√(2π), σ√(2π)) and probability-density normalizations from the same Mathlib integral.

OQ-05-OQ-01 formalizes the polar-coordinate proof that the squared Gaussian integral is π (the area-of-circle identity restated here as gaussian_unit_sq); this entry instead develops the 1D probability-density rescalings.

The multivariate sibling named in this file's header: ∫ e^{-xᵀAx} = √(πⁿ/det A) for positive-definite A, with the diagonal case proved via Fubini and the scalar Gaussian. Its normalization constant √(πⁿ/det A) is the n-dimensional generalization of the σ√(2π) constant derived here — the per-coordinate variances σᵢ√(2π) multiply out to give the determinant factor.

The moment/cumulant generating function of the Gaussian, the natural probabilistic sequel once the density is normalized: the standard-normal MGF and characteristic function ∫ e^{tx}e^{-x²/2} = e^{t²/2}√(2π) carry the very √(2π) prefactor that std_normal_normalization cancels to 1 here.

OQ-05-OQ-03 proves the Gaussian is its own Fourier transform. The self-duality is stated for e^{-x²/2}, the exact integrand normalized here: the √(2π) that makes ∫ (1/√(2π))e^{-x²/2} = 1 is the same constant appearing in the Fourier normalization that makes e^{-x²/2} a fixed point, so this density-normalization strand and the Fourier strand share their one nontrivial constant.

conclusion.summary: The normalization constants of the normal distribution — √(2π), σ√(2π) — and the probability-density normalizations ∫ (1/√(2π))e^{-x²/2} = 1 and ∫ (1/(σ√(2π)))e^{-x²/(2σ²)} = 1 are derived axiom-free from the Gaussian integral ∫ e^{-x²} = √π, together with mean-shift invariance and the area identity (∫ e^{-x²})² = π. The bell curve's constants are exactly √π evaluated at different rates.
conclusion.implications: This completes the elementary 1D strand of the area-of-circle Gaussian-integral lineage with the probability-density normalizations, making explicit the bridge from the geometric Gaussian integral to the normal distribution. The lemmas (rate-matched Gaussian integrals, constant pull-out, mean-shift invariance) are reusable for further probabilistic formalization built on Mathlib's Gaussian API.
openQuestions: Formalize the moments of the standard normal from these normalizations: E[X^{2k}] = (2k−1)!! (double factorial) and E[X^{2k+1}] = 0 by symmetry, obtained by repeated integration by parts against the normalized density (or by differentiating the MGF ∫ e^{tx}·(1/√(2π))e^{-x²/2} = e^{t²/2}).

Prove closure under convolution: the sum of independent N(μ₁,σ₁²) and N(μ₂,σ₂²) is N(μ₁+μ₂, σ₁²+σ₂²). This is the analytic backbone of the central limit theorem and is naturally attacked through the Fourier-transform sibling (oq-05-oq-03) once the density is normalized.

Extend the normalization to the multivariate normal N(0,Σ): the constant (2π)^{n/2}√(det Σ). The diagonal case factors into a product of the scalar σᵢ√(2π) constants derived here (see oq-05-oq-02); the general positive-definite case needs a spectral change of variables.

mainTheorems.name: gaussian_variance_normalization
mainTheorems.description: The N(0,σ²) normalization: ∫ (1/(σ√(2π)))·e^{-x²/(2σ²)} dx = 1 for σ > 0 — the Gaussian is a probability density.

mainTheorems.name: gaussian_variance
mainTheorems.description: General variance Gaussian integral: ∫ e^{-x²/(2σ²)} dx = σ√(2π) for σ > 0, from integral_gaussian at rate 1/(2σ²).
mainTheorems.leanType: ∀ (σ : ℝ), 0 < σ → ∫ x : ℝ, Real.exp (-x ^ 2 / (2 * σ ^ 2)) = σ * Real.sqrt (2 * π)

mainTheorems.name: gaussian_mean_shift
mainTheorems.description: Mean-shift invariance: ∫ e^{-(x-μ)²/2} dx = √(2π) for every μ, by translation invariance of the Lebesgue integral.
mainTheorems.leanType: ∀ (μ : ℝ), ∫ x : ℝ, Real.exp (-(x - μ) ^ 2 / 2) = Real.sqrt (2 * π)
